name: Develop a compact on-device language model optimized for

representative_ideas: Develop a compact on-device language model optimized for software API function calling, enabling privacy-preserving and low-latency tool use
common_problems: Function calling with LLMs requires cloud infrastructure, introducing latency, privacy risks, and dependency on external services
solution_approaches: Design and deploy an on-device language model (Octopus) specifically optimized for software API function calling, enabling direct tool invocation without cloud round-trips
story: Position on-device function calling as the key to unlocking privacy-preserving, real-time AI assistants; frame as democratizing access to intelligent automation by removing infrastructure barriers
application: Mobile apps requiring secure on-device tool execution, IoT devices needing autonomous API interactions, enterprise applications with strict data privacy requirements

title: Octopus: On-device language model for function calling of software APIs

name: Enable coding agents to recover from sub-optimal decisions

representative_ideas: Enable coding agents to recover from sub-optimal decisions through dynamic action re-sampling at key decision points, creating adaptive tree traversal for more efficient inference-time compute scaling
common_problems: LLM-powered coding agents struggle with sub-optimal decision-making during task execution, requiring either extensive manual intervention or inefficient compute scaling through random sampling
solution_approaches: Dynamic Action Re-Sampling (DARS) branches trajectories at key decision points by taking alternative actions given trajectory history and execution feedback from previous attempts, enabling adaptive tree traversal that recovers from sub-optimal paths
story: Reframe coding agent improvement from naive compute scaling into intelligent adaptive tree traversal, where agents dynamically explore alternative decision paths at critical junctures rather than following linear or random trajectories, transforming agents into strategic decision-makers
application: Software engineering automation, coding assistants, debugging assistance, complex development task execution

title: DARS: Dynamic Action Re-Sampling to Enhance Coding Agent Performance by Adaptive Tree Traversal

name: Synthesize diverse virtual scenarios to train agents on

representative_ideas: Synthesize diverse virtual scenarios to train agents on action knowledge refinement, enabling learning beyond limited real-world data
common_problems: Agents cannot acquire diverse action knowledge from limited real-world interactions, restricting their ability to handle novel situations
solution_approaches: Create a virtual scenario synthesis framework (SynWorld) that generates varied scenarios for refining agentic action knowledge
story: Frame virtual scenario synthesis as a paradigm shift from data-limited training to infinite synthetic experience, enabling agents to learn from scenarios that would be dangerous or impossible to encounter in reality
application: Training autonomous vehicles in edge cases, simulating robotic manipulation in diverse environments, preparing agents for rare but critical decision-making scenarios

title: SynWorld: Virtual Scenario Synthesis for Agentic Action Knowledge Refinement

name: Introduce MARS benchmark to evaluate LLMs' ability to

representative_ideas: Introduce MARS benchmark to evaluate LLMs' ability to reason about distributional changes and situational transitions, revealing fundamental gaps in current model capabilities
common_problems: LLMs lack systematic ability to comprehend situational changes and distributional shifts triggered by environmental factors, a fundamental capability for functioning as conscious agents
solution_approaches: Formulate reasoning about distributional changes as a three-step discriminative process (MetAphysical ReaSoning), create benchmark with three tasks assessing action changes, state changes, and situational transitions
story: Elevate metaphysical reasoning from philosophical abstraction to a concrete AI capability gap; frame benchmark as essential for understanding whether LLMs can truly model causality and change in real-world scenarios
application: Evaluating AI assistants for planning and forecasting, assessing models for autonomous decision-making in dynamic environments, benchmarking causal reasoning capabilities

title: MARS: Benchmarking the Metaphysical Reasoning Abilities of Language Models with a Multi-task Evaluation Dataset

name: Introduce step-level trajectory calibration to automatically identify and

representative_ideas: Introduce step-level trajectory calibration to automatically identify and correct suboptimal actions during agent training, addressing error accumulation in long-horizon tasks
common_problems: Existing LLM agent learning methods (behavior cloning, preference learning) fail in long-horizon tasks where suboptimal actions accumulate step-by-step, causing trajectory drift
solution_approaches: STeCa identifies suboptimal actions through step-level reward comparison during exploration, constructs calibrated trajectories using LLM-driven reflection, and leverages these for reinforced training
story: Frame trajectory calibration as a paradigm shift from end-to-end learning to granular error correction; position timely calibration as essential for achieving robust, reliable agent behavior in complex tasks
application: Training agents for multi-step planning tasks, robotics instruction following, autonomous code generation, complex workflow automation

title: STeCa: Step-level Trajectory Calibration for LLM Agent Learning

name: A cost-effective methodology for curating high-quality domain-specific datasets

representative_ideas: A cost-effective methodology for curating high-quality domain-specific datasets from noisy web sources to train specialist LLMs, demonstrated in astronomy with significant performance gains
common_problems: General-purpose LLMs lack depth for expert-level domain tasks due to limited domain-specific information, and domain adaptation requires substantial high-quality data that is expensive and challenging to curate from noisy web sources
solution_approaches: ORBIT methodology filters and refines noisy web data through multi-stage quality assessment to create high-quality domain-specific subsets, demonstrated by refining 1.3T-token FineWeb-Edu into 10B-token astronomy subset for fine-tuning
story: Position domain adaptation as a data engineering challenge requiring systematic curation rather than just model training, presenting a principled methodology that transforms noisy web sources into high-quality specialist training data, enabling expert-level LLM performance
application: Training specialist LLMs for domain-specific tasks in astronomy, law, medicine, and other specialized fields requiring expert knowledge

title: ORBIT: Cost-Effective Dataset Curation for Large Language Model Domain Adaptation with an Astronomy Case Study

name: Identify long-term memory as a critical bottleneck in

representative_ideas: Identify long-term memory as a critical bottleneck in LLM agent systems and propose enhanced memory management through metadata-enriched vector databases and external knowledge integration
common_problems: LLM agents lack effective long-term memory mechanisms; current vector database implementations fail to separate procedural from semantic memory and cannot manage memory over the agent's lifetime
solution_approaches: Review memory management approaches in LLM agents, utilize vector databases for storage and retrieval, propose metadata enrichment for procedural and semantic memory separation, and integrate external knowledge sources
story: Reframe memory from an engineering implementation detail into a fundamental research challenge for achieving autonomous, lifelong learning agents; position memory management as the key enabler for agent scalability and sustained capability
application: Autonomous agents requiring persistent knowledge across sessions, customer service agents accumulating domain expertise, personal assistants maintaining user context over extended periods

title: Memory Matters: The Need to Improve Long-Term Memory in LLM-Agents
